items.stem:
Walking in a straight line and riding a bicycle are the activities which are possible due to a part of the brain. Choose the correct location and name of this part from the given table:
Part of the BrainName
(a)Fore brainCerebrum
(b)Mid brainHypothalamus

items.answer: Walking in a straight line and riding a bicycle are voluntary actions and are controlled by the cerebellum. items.answer: Nerve impulses are always transmitted across a synapse from the axon terminals of one neuron to the dendrite or cell body of the next neuron, never in the reverse direction. Since the neurotransmitter is present only in the axon terminals, it cannot be released from the dendrite or cell body even if the impulse reaches there.

items.stem: Name the chemicals which transmit the information in animals.
items.answer: Hormones.

items.stem: Name the glands which secrete these chemicals.
items.answer: Endocrine glands.

items.stem: Name the scientists who gave the term hormone.
items.answer: The term hormone was given by Bayliss and Starling.

items.stem: The coordination and control of all the hormone-producing glands is lost in a person. Which gland in such an individual may have become non-functional?
items.answer: Pituitary gland.

items.stem: Name the hormone which acts opposite to glucagon.
items.answer: Insulin.

items.stem: Name the endocrine glands which produce gametes.
items.answer: The testes and ovary produce gametes.

items.stem: If you find a large swelling in the neck projecting outward, which category of secretions do you think is being produced in shortage?
items.answer: Thyroxin hormone. Its shortage causes simple goitre.

items.stem: Name the hormone secreted by parathyroid glands and give its one function.
items.answer: The parathyroid secretes calcitonin or parathormone, which regulates blood calcium and phosphate.

items.stem: Which hormone helps in lowering the level of blood glucose in human beings?
items.answer: Insulin helps in lowering the level of blood glucose in human beings.

items.stem: Which hormone is responsible for the development of moustache and beard in man?
items.answer: Testosterone is responsible for the development of moustache and beard in man.

items.stem: Name the disease caused due to failure of insulin secretion.
items.answer: Diabetes mellitus is caused due to failure of insulin secretion.

items.stem: Name a gland associated with brain. Which problem is caused due to the deficiency of the hormone released by this gland?
items.answer: Pituitary gland. Pituitary gland releases growth hormones. The deficiency of this hormone causes stunted growth.

items.stem: Define phototropism.
items.answer: Movement or bending of the shoot towards light is called phototropism.

items.stem: Give an example of plant hormone that promotes growth.
items.answer: Gibberellins helps in the growth of stem.

items.stem: Give examples of chemotropism.
items.answer: The growth of pollen tube towards ovule.

items.stem: Name the part of brain which controls posture and balance of the body.
items.answer: Cerebellum.

items.stem: Name the part of the neuron where information is acquired.
items.answer: Dendrite.

items.stem: How is brain protected from injury and shock?
items.answer: (i) The brain is located inside a bony box called cranium. (ii) The brain is contained in a fluid filled cavity which provides further shock absorption.

items.stem: What is the structural and functional unit of nervous system?
items.answer: Neuron.

items.stem: Name the part of neuron through which the information travels as an electric impulse.
items.answer: Axon.

items.stem: How is the spinal cord protected in human body?
items.answer: Spinal cord is enclosed in a bony cage called vertebral column.

items.stem: List two body functions that will be affected if cerebellum gets damaged.
items.answer: (i) Walking in a straight line. (ii) Picking up a thing from ground.

items.stem: What does the given experimental set-up demonstrate?
items.answer: The given experimental set-up demonstrates, “Response of the plant to the direction of light”.

items.stem: Name one directional growth movement each in response to chemicals and water in plants. Write an example for each of them.
items.answer:
Chemotropism and hydrotropism are the directional growth movements in response to chemicals and water respectively.
Chemotropism example – growth of pollen tube towards the ovule.
Hydrotropism example – growth of roots towards water.

items.stem: What is tropism? Describe the types of tropism. Mention two differences between tropism and nastic movement.
items.answer: Tropism is a change in the direction of a part of a plant in response to a stimulus. Types of tropism: geotropism, phototropism, hydrotropism and chemotropism. Differences - (i) tropism is a slow response to a stimulus while nastic movement is an immediate response; (ii) tropism is directional while nastic movement is non-directional.

items.stem: Why are endocrine glands also called ductless glands?
items.answer: Endocrine glands are called ductless glands because they do not have ducts; they pour their secretions directly into the blood, which carries these hormones to their target organs.

items.stem: List the characteristics of hormones.
items.answer: (i) They are secreted by an endocrine gland. (ii) They are specific chemical regulators. (iii) They are poured directly into the blood and circulated through it. (iv) They act on a specific tissue or organ called the target organ. (v) Their excess or deficiency may lead to serious consequences.

items.stem: Name the endocrine glands found in the human body.
items.answer: (i) Hypothalamus (ii) Pituitary (iii) Pineal (iv) Thyroid (v) Parathyroid (vi) Pancreas (vii) Adrenal (viii) Testis (ix) Ovary.

items.stem: Why is the pituitary gland also called the master gland?
items.answer: The pituitary gland is called the master gland because it controls and coordinates the secretion of all the other endocrine glands.

items.stem: State the main function of the pituitary gland. Write the effect of (i) excessive and (ii) sluggish activity of this gland on the growth of a child.
items.answer: The main function of the pituitary gland is to control the other endocrine glands and the development of bones and muscles. (i) Excessive activity leads to gigantism. (ii) Sluggish activity leads to dwarfism.

items.stem: How does the feedback mechanism regulate hormone secretion? Cite an example to explain the feedback mechanism for regulation of hormonal secretion.
items.answer: The feedback mechanism regulates the timing and amount of hormone secreted. For example, if a person has more sugar in the blood this is detected by the cells of the pancreas, and more insulin is secreted to oxidise the sugar. In the reverse situation, the secretion of insulin is reduced.

items.stem:
Name a hormone secreted by (a) Pancreas, (b) Pituitary, (c) Thyroid. Write one function of each of the hormones.
Name of the glandName of the hormoneFunction
(a)PancreasInsulinIt controls blood sugar level.
(b)PituitaryGrowth hormoneIt regulates growth and development of the body.
(c)ThyroidThyroxineIt regulates metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats.
items.answer: (a) Pancreas - insulin, which controls blood sugar level. (b) Pituitary - growth hormone, which regulates growth and development of the body. (c) Thyroid - thyroxine, which regulates the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats.
